integration_issues.issue: Setting jukebox-volume to 0.3 via input/change events resulted in document.querySelector('audio').volume reporting 0.6 (state may be propagating to a different/secondary <audio> element on the page). Slider, mute, next, clear all render and accept input. Likely either (a) querySelector hit the video-wall audio not jukebox audio, or (b) onChange handler not wiring slider value to <audio ref>. Not blocking but worth verifying that the JukeboxWindow's <audio> element's .volume tracks the slider.

action_items: Verify JukeboxWindow.jsx audio ref .volume is bound to slider state (jukebox-volume) — UI test observed audio.volume=0.6 after slider set to 0.3 (could be unrelated audio el; quick to confirm).

Doc note: review_request mentions sprite IDs as 'tiny_ghost/cute_ghost/giant_ghost' but actual implementation uses 'ghost_tiny/ghost_cute/ghost_giant' (consistent with WS event sample {sprite_id:ghost_tiny}). All 9 sprite-pick-{id} testids exist with the ghost_* prefix variant. No code change needed; just align doc.
critical_code_review_comments: Upload rate limit is in-process per-user dict (_upload_times) — won't share across replicas; OK for single-instance preview but will silently fail-open in scaled deployments.

Streaming download (StreamingResponse) currently buffers the entire file in memory (data, _ = get_object) before chunking. True streaming would require requests.get(..., stream=True) and iter_content. Memory cost equals file size (50MB cap).
/api/guestbook has no rate limit; spammable. Consider a per-user/IP throttle similar to upload.
WS handlers trust client-supplied sprite_id with no validation against SPRITE_IDS allowlist. Worth adding server-side check to prevent garbage in user list.
Typing event has no cooldown — a malicious client could spam typing=true to all peers. Throttle on server side or add a min interval.
MAX_HISTORY_PER_ROOM=50 is fine, but db.messages still has no TTL/cap; flagged in iter1 and still applicable.
Frontend chat-history replay relies entirely on server snapshot.history; no local cache, so offline reconnect shows blank momentarily — acceptable for retro UX.
